title: Reverse Linked List
oneLinerQuestion: Reverse a singly linked list iteratively or recursively.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Reverse Linked List problem asks us to reverse a singly linked list in-place and return the new head pointer. Because nodes in a singly linked list only store a forward `next` reference, overwriting `curr.next` immediately severs access to the remainder of the list. To reverse the direction safely without losing downstream nodes, we maintain three pointers: `prev` to track the already reversed sublist, `curr` for the active node whose link is being redirected, and a temporary pointer `next` to buffer the rest of the list before breaking the forward connection. This enables a clean, linear, in-place transformation in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

- Step 1: Base Case & State Initialization — We initialize two pointer variables: `prev = null` (which acts as the initial tail sentinel) and `curr = head` (pointing to the start of the original list).

- Step 2: Linear Iteration Guard — We execute a while loop `while (curr !== null)` that continues processing until the active node pointer traverses past the final node of the list.

- Step 3: Buffering Next Node Reference — Before redirecting any pointers, we temporarily store the forward link: `const next = curr.next`. This ensures we retain access to the rest of the unreversed list.

- Step 4: Reversing the Current Link — We invert the pointer direction of the current node by pointing it backward: `curr.next = prev`. On the very first node (original head), this points its `next` to `null`, correctly making it the new tail.

- Step 5: Advancing Traversal Pointers — We shift the frame forward by one node: `prev = curr` (advancing the head of the reversed prefix) and `curr = next` (moving to the next unreversed node).

- Step 6: Termination & New Head Return — When `curr` becomes `null`, every node's pointer has been reversed. Pointer `prev` now rests on the former tail node, which serves as the new head of the reversed linked list. We return `prev`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) where N is the number of nodes in the linked list, as each node is visited and redirected exactly once. Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space because pointer manipulations are executed strictly in-place without allocating new nodes or auxiliary containers.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION reverseList(head):
    prev = NULL, curr = head
    WHILE curr IS NOT NULL DO:
        nxt = curr.next
        curr.next = prev
        prev = curr
        curr = nxt
    END WHILE
    RETURN prev
END FUNCTION
